messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert: spike in GPU OOMs and KV cache evictions across shard-us-west-2-4. Error rate increased from 0.3% to 6.8% starting 2024-11-02T09:12Z. Root metric: kv_cache.arena_frag_pct > 75% for >5m. Paging oncall(s) now.

sara (oncall): I’m up. seeing the same in graphs. L4 latency for generation jumps to 1.8s median and tail is massive. Any recent deploys or config pushes?

jordan (infra): There was a batching config push to reduce latency earlier this morning (rollout id: batch-opt-2024-11-02). It changed continuous_batch.max_tokens from 4096 -> 8192 and enabled prefix_kv_cache:true for a subset of traffic.

kevin (runtime): That rollout matches the timing. Increasing batch token cap leads to larger KV allocations; when combined with our allocator arena sizing we can hit fragmentation cliffs. Logs show repeated cudaMalloc failures followed by fallback OOM. Example from 09:15Z:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.2 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 24.1 GiB already allocated)
backtrace: ... kv_arena_alloc -> arena_grow -> cudaMalloc 
```

maya (eng-sre): Customer impact: a handful of mid-tier customers reported failed API calls and increased latencies ~09:13-09:40Z. Support tickets 1234, 1235 opened. CS is triaging.

customer-support: Confirmed. Two customers hit 5xx and retried; one elevated. We routed them to Dedicated fallback but they saw degraded throughput.

incident-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-frag. Suggested immediate actions: 1) Rollback batch-opt-2024-11-02 or 2) Temporarily reduce continuous_batch.max_tokens to 2048 for affected rollout.

sara (oncall): I can rollback the rollout. Before doing that, can we do a faster mitigation with allocator env toggles? Kevin, do we have a safe MALLOC_CONF or PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF change that reduces fragmentation without full restart?

kevin (runtime): We can set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 on the running workers; that tends to reduce fragmentation by encouraging smaller splits. However, this env var is only picked up on process start for our current CUDA allocator. So we'd need a rolling restart of the runtime pods. That’s slower than a config rollback.

jordan (infra): Rolling restart plan: cordon node -> restart runtime pod -> let traffic drain -> uncordon. With autoscaling we might temporarily lose capacity. Rollback of the rollout can be instant — we have a single-flag gate.

maya (eng-sre): Given customer impact, I recommend rollback as fastest path. We can follow with a controlled rollout with smaller batch increases and monitor arena metrics.

sara (oncall): Agreed. Initiating rollback of batch-opt-2024-11-02 now. @jordan please watch for deployment health and OOMs.

jordan (infra): Rolling back... command run:
```
redwoodctl rollout cancel batch-opt-2024-11-02 --env=prod --force
```
Monitoring health.

incident-bot: Rollback acknowledged by CI at 2024-11-02T09:22Z. Canary groups set to 0% traffic.

kevin (runtime): I'm seeing immediate drop in new cudaMalloc failures on the affected hosts. Arena fragmentation still high but evictions decrease. Might need to run arena compaction to reclaim free slabs.

maya (eng-sre): Can we trigger compaction safely? Any impact?

kevin (runtime): We have a background compaction path exposed as an admin endpoint: POST /admin/kv/arena/compact which does incremental merges. Recommend running once on the worst hosts. It’s low-risk but CPU/PCIe traffic spikes for a minute.

jordan (infra): Running compaction on hosts us-west-2-4-a,b now. Command: 
```
curl -X POST https://admin.prod.internal/admin/kv/arena/compact -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"max_ms":2000}'
```

customer-support: Noting this in the incident page so CS can update customers.

incident-bot: Compaction jobs started at 2024-11-02T09:27Z. Monitoring eviction and OOM graphs.

maya (eng-sre): After compaction and rollback we still have intermittent tail latencies for ~12 minutes; by 09:40Z metrics show recovery to baseline. We should keep the incident open for a postmortem and longer monitoring window.

sara (oncall): I'm handing off to maya for post-incident follow-up and to own the postmortem. I’ll stay available for any escalations. Handoff note: rollback initiated, compaction run, customers notified.

maya (eng-sre): Taking over. Action items I’m creating: 
- owner: maya, task: write postmortem (due 48h)
- owner: kevin, task: propose allocator tuning (max_split_size_mb/arena sizing) and safe compaction schedule
- owner: jordan, task: add safer rollout guard rails (auto-limit batch-size increase, perf-experiment gating)
- owner: customer-support, task: follow-up with affected customers and document incident timeline

kevin (runtime): Quick note: we should consider a metric alert on continuous_batch.max_tokens increases in prod alongside arena_frag_pct. That would have correlated earlier.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2 at 2024-11-02T09:30Z. PagerDuty: incident-789 created and assigned to oncall.

pagerduty: Reminder: please ack the incident in PD if you’ve taken action.

customer-support: Customers updated with interim mitigation and ETA for postmortem. One requested compensation; CS will escalate to biz ops.

maya (eng-sre): Note for postmortem: include reproducer steps (local harness with max_tokens bump), artifact list (cuda logs, kv arena histograms, rollout diff), timeline (deploy -> spike -> rollback -> compaction -> recovery).

sara (oncall): Closing the active paging loop from oncall perspective; handing to maya. I’ll mark incident-thread as acknowledged and move to follow-ups. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: degraded -> mitigated at 2024-11-02T09:40Z. Postmortem owner: maya.

maya (eng-sre): I’ll open the postmortem doc and ping relevant folks. Reassigning follow-ups in Jira. If anyone has extra logs or customer notes drop them here or attach to the incident doc.
